source.title: A review of four decades of time-dependent scheduling: main results, new topics, and open problems

accepted.question_text: Given n jobs to be processed on a single machine, where job j has linearly deteriorating time-dependent processing time p_j(t) = 1 + b_j t when it starts at time t, and where C_j is the completion time of job j in a schedule, determine the computational complexity of finding a schedule that minimizes the total completion time sum_j C_j. Is this problem polynomial-time solvable, or can it be proved NP-hard at least in the ordinary sense?

evidence.quote: Problem 1|p j= 1+b j t|P C j

accepted.question_text: For the single-machine problem with processing times p_j(t) = 1 + b_j t and objective sum_j C_j, let beta_j = 1 + b_j be the deterioration-rate factor sequence. Suppose this sequence is regular, such as an arithmetic sequence, geometric sequence, or Fibonacci sequence. Algorithm 7.2 constructs a V-shaped schedule in O(n) time by using the periodic sign behavior of the signature S^-(beta), rather than recomputing that signature during the greedy construction. Does Algorithm 7.2 always generate an optimal schedule for every regular sequence of deterioration-rate factors?
accepted.context_brief: Optimality of Algorithm 7.2 for regular sequences

accepted.question_text: Given n jobs to be scheduled on a single machine with arbitrary precedence constraints represented by an acyclic directed graph, where job j has proportional time-dependent processing time p_j(t) = b_j t when it starts at time t, job j has weight w_j, and C_j is its completion time, determine the computational complexity of minimizing the total weighted completion time sum_j w_j C_j. Is this precedence-constrained problem NP-hard at least in the ordinary sense, or is there a polynomial-time algorithm?
accepted.context_brief: Proportional deterioration with precedence and weighted completion

evidence.quote: 1|p j=b j t, prec|P w j C j

accepted.question_text: Given n jobs to be scheduled on a single machine with arbitrary precedence constraints represented by an acyclic directed graph, where job j has linearly deteriorating processing time p_j(t) = a_j + b_j t when it starts at time t, determine the computational complexity of minimizing the makespan C_max = max_j C_j. Is this precedence-constrained linearly deteriorating scheduling problem NP-hard at least in the ordinary sense, or is it polynomial-time solvable?
accepted.context_brief: Linear deterioration with precedence and makespan

evidence.quote: 1|p j=a j+b j t, prec|C max

accepted.question_text: Given n jobs to be scheduled on m identical parallel machines, where job j has time-dependent processing time p_j(t) = a_j + f(t) when it starts at time t, with a_j job-specific and f a common function of starting time, determine the computational complexity of minimizing the makespan C_max. In particular, identify assumptions on f(t), beyond the already known necessary optimality condition, that yield polynomial-time solvable cases, or prove hardness for the general problem.
accepted.context_brief: Parallel machines with additive common time function

evidence.quote: Problem P m|p j=a j+f(t)|C max is open

accepted.question_text: Given n jobs to be scheduled on m identical parallel machines, where job j has time-dependent processing time p_j(t) = b_j f(t) when it starts at time t, with b_j job-specific and f a common function of starting time, determine whether minimizing the total completion time sum_j C_j is polynomial-time solvable under assumptions analogous to those studied for P_m | p_j = a_j + f(t) | C_max, or establish its computational complexity.
accepted.context_brief: Parallel machines with multiplicative common time function

evidence.quote: problem P m|p j= b j f(t)|P C j

accepted.question_text: Given n jobs to be processed on a single machine, where job j has proportional time-dependent processing time p_j(t) = b_j t when it starts at time t and tardiness T_j = max(C_j - d_j, 0) relative to due date d_j, determine the computational complexity of minimizing total tardiness sum_j T_j. Is the problem NP-hard at least in the ordinary sense, as conjectured from the fixed-processing-time counterpart, or is there a polynomial-time algorithm?
accepted.context_brief: Single-machine proportional deterioration and total tardiness

evidence.quote: problem 1|p j=b j t|P T j

accepted.question_text: Given a two-machine flow shop in which each job has one operation on each machine and operation i of job j has proportional time-dependent processing time p_ij(t) = b_ij t when it starts at time t, determine the computational complexity of minimizing total completion time sum_j C_j. Is this two-machine flow-shop time-dependent scheduling problem NP-hard at least in the ordinary sense, or can it be solved in polynomial time?
accepted.context_brief: Two-machine flow shop with proportional operations

evidence.quote: F 2|p ij =b ij t|P C j

accepted.question_text: Given a two-machine open shop in which each job has one operation on each machine and operation i of job j has proportional time-dependent processing time p_ij(t) = b_ij t when it starts at time t, determine the computational complexity of minimizing total completion time sum_j C_j. Is this two-machine open-shop time-dependent scheduling problem NP-hard at least in the ordinary sense, or can it be solved in polynomial time?
accepted.context_brief: Two-machine open shop with proportional operations

evidence.quote: O 2|p ij =b ij t|P C j

accepted.question_text: Given a two-machine flow shop in which each job has one operation on each machine and operation i of job j has proportional-linear time-dependent processing time p_ij(t) = b_ij(a + b t) when it starts at time t, with common constants a and b and operation-specific coefficient b_ij, determine the computational complexity of minimizing total completion time sum_j C_j. Is this problem NP-hard at least in the ordinary sense, or can it be solved in polynomial time?
accepted.context_brief: Two-machine flow shop with proportional-linear operations

evidence.quote: F 2|p ij = b ij (a+bt)|P C j

accepted.question_text: Given a two-machine open shop in which each job has one operation on each machine and operation i of job j has proportional-linear time-dependent processing time p_ij(t) = b_ij(a + b t) when it starts at time t, with common constants a and b and operation-specific coefficient b_ij, determine the computational complexity of minimizing total completion time sum_j C_j. Is this problem NP-hard at least in the ordinary sense, or can it be solved in polynomial time?
accepted.context_brief: Two-machine open shop with proportional-linear operations
